Tobacco Society
The Tobacco Society performs an annual planting ceremony in the spring. The seeds are not those used for smoking, but rather are a species of plant life considered quite holy being associated with the stars and sun. Given to the Crows by Old Man Coyote, it is stated that as long as the Crow Tribe has this ceremony they will continue to exist as the Crow Tribe. Although there are numerous social activities related to the Tobacco Society held throughout the year, its primary function is strictly religious. Membership in the Society is by adoption, married couples usually being adopted together.
Hand Games - Arrow Games
Two aboriginal cultural functions remaining today are the hand game and arrow games, both of which are social functions occuring when the Tribe gathers to place bets on favorite players and do some serious gambling. The various Reservation Districts compete against one another.
In the hand game, players on one team hide objects in their hands and a member of the other team attempts to guess which hand holds the object. Between the teams are a number of sticks; the team guessing successfully collects a tolly stick until one side has all the sticks and win the game.
